questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of synchronized lazy paging, cross-process visibility, and NUMA-aware fairness in a realistic kernel path.

## Key Concepts
- Per-page state machine (idle/in-flight/ready)
- CAS-based owner election to avoid duplicative work
- Notification via wait queues and memory barriers
- Source selection: IO, zero-fill, read-ahead, with fairness under contention
- NUMA affinity and cross-core contention

## Code Example
```c
// sketch: per-page state and atomic owner
typedef struct {
  atomic_int owner; // PID or thread id, 0 = none
  atomic_int state; // 0 idle, 1 in-flight, 2 ready
  // ... other fields
} page_t;
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test for livelock under high contention?
- How would you extend this to support prefetch hints and read-ahead when multiple faults occur?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests understanding of crash-consistency mechanisms, journaling design patterns, and recovery strategies in filesystems. It evaluates how candidates ensure atomic metadata updates and maintain data integrity across power failures.

## Key Concepts
- Write-ahead logging (WAL) and journaling principles
- Two-phase commit protocols for atomic operations
- Recovery procedures and log replay semantics
- Fsync semantics and write ordering guarantees
- Crash scenario handling and partial write detection

## Code Example
```c
typedef struct {
    uint64_t lsn;     // Log sequence number
    uint32_t op;      // Operation type (create, delete, etc.)
    uint32_t ino;     // Inode number
    uint32_t parent;  // Parent directory inode
} log_entry_t;

void log_append(log_entry_t *entries, size_t count);
void log_commit(uint64_t lsn);
```
